entry.note: Identified from the arXiv title page (arXiv:2501.00914v2, math.GT, 13 Mar 2026): Baldwin and Sivek, 'L-spaces and knot traces', 37 pp, 21 sections. No ref() entry, none created (tangential).

relevance.rationale: Four-dimensional knot detection via traces X_n(K) = B^4 ∪ (n-framed 2-handle along K) and Heegaard Floer homology. Read: Introduction and §1.1 (Thm 1.2 the 0-trace detects every L-space knot; Thm 1.3 any trace detects whether a knot is an L-space knot and its genus; Thm 1.4 L-space knots with diffeomorphic 0-surgeries are equal — via Lee–Taubes / Kutluhan–Lee–Taubes symplectic-Floer ↔ HF of the mapping torus; Thm 1.5 positive torus knots are detected by every n-trace with n ≤ 0; Thm 1.6 the positive-trace case for T_{2,2g+1} up to a knot-Floer coincidence). Corpus-grep, all surfaces: zero hits for 'L-space', 'knot trace', 'characterizing slope', 'Heegaard Floer', 'HFK'. The folio's knot invariants are the Jones / Markov trace tr_M of a braid closure in H_n(q) and the hyperbolic gluing data; it has no Floer theory and no 4-manifold layer. Homonym trap worth recording: 'knot trace' (the 4-manifold) is unrelated to the folio's 'Markov trace' and 'trace field', so a corpus-grep on 'trace' lands falsely. The nearest contact — §2's fixed-point-free monodromy (FFPF) criterion for fibred knots, alongside the NZ-from-braid chain's use of the figure-eight fibre monodromy — is a Floer-theoretic input, not a gluing datum, and nothing here changes the corpus's monodromy computation. Scope-(a): as read, supplies nothing usable.
